mode.title: Mode
mode.description: tag = articles for a topic, with clap counts (about 35 per tag). author = an author's recent articles, with clap counts (about 10). publication = a publication's latest articles including the article text, but without clap counts - that is all the source exposes for publications. post = one article with its full text. reference = check the source is live and report what each surface returns.
enumTitles: tag - articles for a topic, with claps
author - an author's articles, with claps
publication - a publication's latest, with text
reference - is the source live, what does it return

tag.title: Tag (tag mode)
tag.description: A Medium topic. A name, a slug or a /tag/ URL all work, e.g. 'artificial-intelligence', 'Machine Learning'.

tags.title: Tags (tag mode)
tags.description: Several topics in one run. One request each, about 35 articles per topic.

tagSection.title: Which part of the tag page
tagSection.description: top = the main tag page, the largest set (about 35 articles). archive = the newest (about 20). recommended = the source's own picks (about 10).

author.title: Author (author mode)
author.description: A Medium handle or profile URL, e.g. '@medium'.

authors.title: Authors (author mode)
authors.description: Several authors in one run, about 10 articles each.

publication.title: Publication (publication mode)
publication.description: A publication slug or URL, e.g. 'better-programming'.

publications.title: Publications (publication mode)
publications.description: Several publications in one run, 10 articles each.

postUrls.title: Article URLs (post mode)
postUrls.description: Several articles in one run. One request each.

maxItems.title: Max items
maxItems.description: Maximum records per run. A tag yields about 35 articles, an author or a publication about 10.

maxConcurrency.title: Max concurrency
maxConcurrency.description: How many pages to fetch in parallel.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Residential proxy is on by default. The source sits behind a protection layer that answers ordinary connections but tends to challenge datacenter addresses, so leave this on for scheduled runs.
